findings.issue_text: [BUG] The Lithuanian totpStep1 value was replaced with Italian text ('Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'), not a Lithuanian translation. Lithuanian users see an Italian instruction string in the account console; the change silently degrades the lt locale instead of fixing it, and the sanitizer passes it because it contains no HTML.

[BUG] The zh_CN (Simplified Chinese) totpStep1 value was replaced with Traditional Chinese text ('在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：'). Simplified-Chinese users receive Traditional-Chinese text in the account console; the locale file no longer matches its declared language.

[ADVISORY] POLICY_SOME_HTML whitelists only br/p/strong/b, so any translation mirroring an English message that uses any other tag (e.g. <i>, <em>, <code>, <ul>, <h3>) is stripped and flagged as illegal HTML, failing the build. The next contributor adding a legitimate translation of an existing English message that uses a tag outside the four-element whitelist gets a hard MojoExecutionException-style build failure with a confusing 'Illegal HTML' message, and must either extend the whitelist or add another key-specific carve-out in normalizeValue (which already accumulates special cases for templateHelp, optimizeLookupHelp, linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit, error-invalid-multivalued-size).

[ADVISORY] verifySafeHtml throws a raw RuntimeException (not MojoExecutionException) when the derived English file is missing, escaping the IOException catch in verify(). When a new community locale file is added whose English counterpart does not exist at the string-mangled path (replaceAll("resources-community","resources") + regex _[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties), the verifier crashes with an unhandled RuntimeException instead of a diagnosable MojoExecutionException naming the missing prerequisite, and the regex-based English-path derivation silently produces a wrong path for any filename pattern not matching _<locale>.properties.

[BUG] verifySafeHtml() throws a bare RuntimeException when the derived English counterpart file does not exist, crashing the Maven build instead of reporting a per-file validation message. For any community locale properties file whose _en counterpart is absent or at an unexpected path (e.g., a community-only translation file, or a fixture/locale naming the replaceAll regex mishandles), FileInputStream throws FileNotFoundException, wrapped in RuntimeException('unable to read file'), which verify() does not catch (it only catches IOException) and which bypasses the MojoExecutionException error-reporting convention, aborting the build with a stack trace rather than the structured messages list.

[ADVISORY] No test exercises the positive path: a translation whose English source contains HTML and whose translation uses the same allowed tags is never verified to pass. The core acceptance criterion 'HTML is permitted in a translation if and only if the English source has HTML' is only tested from the failing side (illegalHtmlTag_en, noHtml_de). A regression that makes the sanitizer reject all HTML-bearing translations (e.g., an asymmetry between the unescapeHtml4 normalization and the sanitizer's entity escaping, or POLICY_SOME_HTML not covering a tag English legitimately uses) would fail the build across every real theme file and would not be caught by any test in this diff.

[ADVISORY] All four hardcoded normalizeValue whitelists (templateHelp, optimizeLookupHelp, linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit/error-invalid-multivalued-size, and the email-only RTL-style strip) are untested in this diff. These key-specific escape hatches are load-bearing for the real theme files changed in this same diff (messages_en.properties's error-invalid-multivalued-size uses a {2,choice,...} pattern; zh_CN templateHelp relies on the CLAIM.<NAME> carve-out), yet no fixture covers any of them; a regression in the regexes would surface only as build failures on production theme files that CI test fixtures do not represent.

[ADVISORY] santizeAnchors mutates `value` with replaceFirst (removing the first occurrence) while iterating a Matcher bound to the pre-mutation string, so repeated or reordered identical anchor tags desynchronize matching. A translation that legitimately contains the same anchor tag as the English source but appears more times than in English (or where an earlier identical anchor was already consumed) gets its first occurrence removed instead of the matched one, and subsequent iterations either falsely report "Didn't find anchor tag ... in original string" or silently leave an unvalidated anchor in the value that POLICY_SOME_HTML (which does not allow 'a') will then strip, producing a misleading mismatch diff for translators.

[ADVISORY] containsHtml() only recognizes lowercase tags via <[a-z]+[^>]*>, so uppercase or unusual tag spellings in the English source are treated as no-HTML. An English message containing e.g.
or

selects POLICY_NO_HTML, and the matching translation is then rejected as 'Illegal HTML' even though it mirrors the English markup — an obvious edge case no section of the diff addresses and no test covers; translators get a false build failure keyed to an uppercase variant of an allowed tag.

[ADVISORY] verify() now reads and parses the properties file twice (Files.readString for duplicate-key checking, then a second FileInputStream+PropertyResourceBundle for the HTML check) and mixes two error conventions (MojoExecutionException for one, raw RuntimeException for the other). Every file verified pays a redundant full read/parse on the build hot path, and the next maintainer adding a failure mode must choose between two incompatible exception styles in the same method; the file is additionally parsed with two different mechanisms whose property-escaping semantics must stay in lockstep for the duplicate-key and HTML checks to agree on the same key set.

[ADVISORY] The English-counterpart path is derived by string surgery (replaceAll of 'resources-community' and of the locale suffix) rather than from the actual set of resource files, so any layout variant silently self-compares. For a file where the regex does not rewrite the suffix as expected (e.g., a properties file without a _xx locale segment, or a path containing an underscore pattern the character class handles differently), englishFile resolves to the file itself; the comparison then trivially passes and the file's HTML is validated only against itself, giving the author of a bad English source string a green build with no indication that the cross-language consistency check never actually ran.

[BUG] The Lithuanian totpStep1 value was replaced with Italian text ('Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'), so Lithuanian users get an Italian instruction on the account page. Lithuanian users see an Italian sentence for the OTP setup step; the LT community translation is corrupted and any downstream translation tooling will diff it against the wrong language.

[BUG] The zh_CN (Simplified Chinese) totpStep1 value was replaced with Traditional Chinese text ('在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：'), which is the zh_TW script in a zh_CN resource. Simplified-Chinese users receive a Traditional-Chinese string; the locale file now contradicts its own locale code and will confuse future zh_CN translation contributions and QA.

[ADVISORY] The totpStep1 rewrite across fi/lt/sk/sv/zh_CN strips the app names and store links and replaces them with a bare 'install one of the following apps:' lead-in, degrading message content purely so the strings pass the new verifier rather than as a translation-quality change. Users in these locales lose the actionable app/store information the English source still conveys (totpStep1 in messages_en retains the FreeOTP/Google Play links); localizers following the new linter will keep dropping links, and nothing in the verifier requires or reviews this content loss.

[ADVISORY] The error-invalid-multivalued-size change converts {{0}}-style placeholders to ICU {0,choice,...} plural syntax in two unrelated UI message bundles (account and admin), which is a message-format feature change, not HTML sanitization work. A pluralization behavior change ships inside an 'HTML sanitizer' PR: any consumer of these bundles that does not support ChoiceFormat (or a theme override still using {{0}}) renders the raw choice pattern to users, and the change is untraceable to the sanitizer requirement except via the normalizeValue() workaround that had to be added for it.

[ADVISORY] verifySafeHtml() hard-codes the 'CLAIM.<NAME>' and '<Extensions>' exceptions and the email RTL strip inline in normalizeValue(), so each new legitimate '<...>' occurrence in a message requires another key-specific branch in the verifier plus a matching .properties edit in this PR (as already done for templateHelp in messages_zh_CN). Every future translation that legitimately mentions an angle-bracket placeholder trips the build for all contributors until someone adds another if-branch here; the exception list grows without a single source of truth and is invisible to translation tooling.

[BUG] The Lithuanian totpStep1 message was replaced with Italian text ('Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:') in messages_lt.properties. Lithuanian-speaking users configuring OTP see an Italian instruction in the Lithuanian UI; the localization is wrong at runtime for every account page render.

[BUG] The zh_CN (Simplified Chinese) totpStep1 message was replaced with Traditional Chinese text ('在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：'). The Simplified Chinese locale renders Traditional Chinese characters, which is a localization-correctness defect for all zh_CN users on the OTP setup step.

[BUG] The rewritten totpStep1 strings across fi/lt/sk/sv/zh_CN all end with 'install one of the following applications:' but no list of applications follows — totpStep2 ('Open the app and scan the QR code') is the next message, so the instruction references a list that does not exist. Users in these locales are told to pick from a list of apps that is never shown, making the instruction unactionable; the prior text at least named FreeOTP/Google Authenticator inline.

[ADVISORY] normalizeValue hardcodes per-key exemptions ('templateHelp', 'optimizeLookupHelp', 'error-invalid-multivalued-size', 'linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit') as string-keyed branches inside the verifier instead of a data-driven allowlist. Every future translation that legitimately needs '<' or angle-bracket text requires a code change and re-release of the verifier; each new special case also risks colliding with other keys whose values happen to contain the same pattern, and the next contributor will not know these exemptions exist.

[ADVISORY] containsHtml uses Pattern '<[a-z]+[^>]*>' which only matches lowercase tag names, so English source strings containing uppercase tags like '' or '

' are classified as no-HTML. A translation using the same uppercase tag as its English source is flagged as 'Illegal HTML' even though it mirrors the source exactly, producing false build failures that translators cannot resolve without editing the verifier.

[ADVISORY] verifySafeHtml throws a raw RuntimeException('unable to read file') instead of MojoExecutionException, unlike the surrounding verify() error handling, and re-reads the file a second time after verify() already loaded it with Files.readString. A missing/unreadable English counterpart file aborts the Maven plugin with an untyped RuntimeException rather than the plugin's declared failure type, giving operators an inconsistent error surface; the double read is wasted IO per properties file on every build.

[ADVISORY] getEnglishValue silently returns an empty string when the key is missing from the English bundle, so the translation is checked under POLICY_NO_HTML and any HTML in it is reported as 'Illegal HTML in key ...'. When the real problem is a translation key that has no English counterpart (or a mis-derived englishFile path), the maintainer chases an 'illegal HTML' message that names the wrong root cause; the missing-English-key condition is never surfaced.

[ADVISORY] santizeAnchors only verifies that anchors present in the translation also exist in the English source; a translation that silently drops the English anchor tags passes verification. A translator can omit the '<a href=...>' link (e.g. the email-confirmation link) from a translated message and the build stays green, shipping locales where users receive instructions referencing a link that is not there; the check is one-directional by design but nothing else catches the loss.

[ADVISORY] The new tests cover illegal tag, no-HTML, and changed-anchor cases but none exercise the normalizeValue special cases (choice-format stripping for error-invalid-multivalued-size, CLAIM.<NAME> for templateHelp, <Extensions> for optimizeLookupHelp) or the English-file-derived-path logic. A regression in the key-specific normalization (e.g. the choice-format regex) would fail the verifier against the real message bundles in this very diff (the {2,choice,...} entry in messages_en.properties), and no test in the diff would have caught it; coverage gap on the newest, most intricate logic added here.

[BUG] The Lithuanian totpStep1 message was replaced with Italian text ('Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'), so Lithuanian users now see an Italian sentence. Lithuanian-language account UI renders an Italian instruction line for OTP setup; this content change was smuggled in to satisfy the new HTML verifier and is not a translation of the English source, silently changing the product's localized content without translator/human acceptance.

[BUG] The zh_CN (Simplified Chinese) totpStep1 value was replaced with Traditional Chinese text (手機/應用程式), switching the script of the locale. Simplified Chinese users are shown Traditional Chinese characters in the OTP setup message; the rewrite needed to pass the new sanitizer introduced a wrong-locale string (likely copied from zh_TW) that was never explicitly accepted as a translation change.

[ADVISORY] The PR bundles wholesale rewrites of translated strings in at least five locales (fi, lt, sk, sv, zh_CN totpStep1) plus HTML-fragment repairs (da, nl, uk, fa, hu, tr, no and all the
→
files) into a 'add HTML sanitizer' infrastructure change. Translators and locale maintainers reviewing by path will see a lint-tool PR, not a translation change; the objective drifted from 'add a verifier' to 'rewrite community translations', and the two wrong-language regressions (lt, zh_CN) show these rewrites bypassed any translation review. These content edits should be separated into a translator-reviewable change.

[ADVISORY] normalizeValue() hardcodes per-key special cases ('templateHelp', 'optimizeLookupHelp', 'linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*', 'error-invalid-multivalued-size') as an if/else chain, so every new message containing angle brackets or choice formats will require another hand-added branch here. Each future translation containing a literal <...> placeholder breaks CI until a maintainer adds another key-specific carve-out; the exception list is hand-maintained parallel state to the message files with no test guarding the list itself, and contributors cannot discover it without reading the verifier source.

[ADVISORY] The '***' prefix was removed from the key '***emailUpdateConfirmationBodyHtml', silently activating a message value that was previously an inert, unparsed key. Hungarian email-update-confirmation HTML mails change from falling back to the base English template to using this long-unmaintained Hungarian string; because the key previously did not exist as a resource, no reviewer of the original translation ever accepted this text as live product content.

[ADVISORY] verifySafeHtml() is invoked unconditionally inside verify() and throws a bare RuntimeException (not MojoExecutionException) when the derived _en.properties counterpart file is missing, changing the existing failure contract of verify(). Any locale file whose English path derivation (replaceAll('resources-community','resources') + regex rename) does not produce an existing file now fails the whole Maven build with an unclassified RuntimeException instead of a per-file message, and the previous verify() contract (returning a messages list, wrapping IOException in MojoExecutionException) is silently broken for that case.

[BUG] verifySafeHtml throws a raw RuntimeException (not MojoExecutionException) when the derived English counterpart file does not exist, aborting the whole Maven build with a wrapped FileNotFoundException instead of a reportable plugin error. Any properties file processed by the verifier whose English file path (derived via replaceAll("resources-community","resources")) is missing crashes the build with an internal RuntimeException; no test in the diff covers the missing-English-file path, so this failure mode ships unexercised.

[ADVISORY] getEnglishValue silently maps a missing English key to the empty string, so the anchor check and the HTML policy for that key are evaluated against a nonexistent source. When an English key is renamed or removed, every translation of that key containing anchors fails the build with 'Didn't find anchor tag' false positives, and the NO_HTML policy is applied to a value whose true English source was never consulted — contributors get misleading diagnostics pointing at the translation instead of the real drift in the English file.

[ADVISORY] normalizeValue hardcodes a per-key escape hatch list (templateHelp, optimizeLookupHelp, linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit, error-invalid-multivalued-size, plus the email RTL strip) that must be manually kept in sync with message content across all theme files. Every future English/translated message that legitimately contains '<' outside real markup (e.g. a new MessageFormat choice pattern or a placeholder like <NAME>) breaks the build until this hand-maintained list is extended; the pressure this creates is to widen POLICY_SOME_HTML, which directly weakens the HTML control this PR exists to enforce.

[ADVISORY] The containsHtml gate is a single coarse regex (<[a-z]+[^>]*>) over the whole English value, so any tag anywhere in the English string unlocks POLICY_SOME_HTML (p/br/strong/b) for the entire translation of that key. A translator can add bold/paragraph markup anywhere in a message whose English source merely contains one unrelated tag; combined with the per-instance (non-static) PolicyFactory fields this is not exploitable for XSS — the OWASP sanitizer still strips everything outside the four allowed elements — but it widens the accepted markup surface beyond what the per-message intent is, and the enforcement relies on the exact-string comparison surviving sanitizer normalization quirks (the many
→
edits across locale files in this same diff are evidence of that fragility).

[ADVISORY] Every new test asserts only that some message contains a substring; no test exercises the positive path where verify() must return an empty list for a valid file (legal HTML allowed because English source contains HTML, matching anchor tags, choice-format normalization). A regression that makes the sanitizer flag every translation (e.g. over-aggressive entity unescaping or anchor matching) leaves all four tests passing — the build still fails on the real theme files, so CI green/red signals are decoupled from test outcomes and the new 'allowed HTML' contract is unverified.

[ADVISORY] No test fixture triggers the normalizeValue branches for templateHelp, optimizeLookupHelp, or the {n,choice,...} replacement used for error-invalid-multivalued-size and linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit — the new special-case allowlist code in the diff has zero coverage. A typo in any of these regexes (e.g. the [A-Z]* quantifier or the choice pattern) ships undetected; the next contributor adding a new translation with these keys discovers it only via a broken full-repo theme-verification build, not via unit tests.

[ADVISORY] The illegalHtmlTag fixture's only key is 'Some
tag...
, which is the actual common case for rogue HTML in translations. If the sanitizer comparison or POLICY_SOME_HTML element allowlist logic is later changed such that well-formed disallowed elements slip through while truncated ones are still caught, verifyIllegalHtmlTagDetected continues to pass and the sanitizer's core guarantee regresses silently.

[ADVISORY] The verifyNoHtmlAllowed test name is misleading: it actually tests that HTML in a translation is rejected when the English source has no HTML, but nothing tests that HTML identical to the English source is accepted — the POLICY_SOME_HTML path is exercised only via the negative illegalHtmlTag case. The POLICY_SOME_HTML allowlist (br/p/strong/b) has no test pinning which tags are allowed; tightening the allowlist (e.g. removing 'p') breaks every legitimate translated email message with no failing unit test to catch it.

[BUG] The Lithuanian totpStep1 translation is replaced with Italian text ('Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'), overwriting a valid Lithuanian translation with content in the wrong language. Lithuanian users see an Italian instruction string in the account UI; the previous correct Lithuanian translation is silently lost with no record, and the string no longer corresponds to the English source it was translated from.

[BUG] The Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) totpStep1 translation is replaced with Traditional Chinese text ('在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一'), silently destroying the Simplified Chinese translation. Simplified Chinese users are shown Traditional Chinese characters; the existing zh_CN translation is overwritten with wrong-locale content and the change is unrecoverable from the diff itself.

[ADVISORY] getEnglishValue swallows MissingResourceException and returns an empty string, so any key present only in a translation file is checked against an empty English source. A translation whose key is missing from the English bundle is silently validated under POLICY_NO_HTML with no anchor comparison; translators get a misleading 'Illegal HTML' error (or, for tag-free values, a silent pass) instead of a 'key missing from English source' diagnostic, hiding real sync drift between bundles.

[ADVISORY] normalizeValue hardcodes an ever-growing per-key allowlist (templateHelp, optimizeLookupHelp, linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit, error-invalid-multivalued-size) of strings whose angle brackets must be pre-stripped before sanitization. Every future message key containing a literal '<...>' or a MessageFormat choice pattern requires a code change to this verifier, and any key author forgets to add breaks the build with an 'Illegal HTML' error; this parallel hand-maintained list will drift as messages are added, and the next contributor inherits an undocumented coupling between message content and verifier source.

[ADVISORY] verifySafeHtml throws a bare RuntimeException on IOException (including the computed English file not existing) instead of the MojoExecutionException the rest of verify() uses. When the derived English path (replaceAll of 'resources-community'/'_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties') misses — e.g. a properties file whose filename pattern doesn't match the language-suffix regex — the Maven build dies with a raw stack trace from inside an iterator lambda instead of the plugin's normal 'Can not read file' error, making CI failures hard to diagnose for exactly the unexpected-file cases the string-munging path derivation is most likely to get wrong.

[BUG] The Lithuanian totpStep1 translation was replaced with Italian text ('Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'), not Lithuanian. Lithuanian users on the account OTP setup page are shown an Italian instruction sentence they likely cannot read; the wrong-language string ships to production.

[BUG] The Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) totpStep1 translation was replaced with Traditional Chinese text ('在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：'), not Simplified Chinese. Simplified Chinese users are served a Traditional Chinese message with different character forms (手機/應用程式 vs 手机/应用程序), a visible locale-contract violation on the OTP setup page.

[BUG] The diff-highlighting loop computes start and end independently, so start can exceed value.length()-end and value.substring(start, value.length()-end) throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. For inputs where the sanitizer output is a proper subsequence overlapping the shared prefix/suffix (e.g. value 'aa' vs sanitized 'a': start=1, end=2, substring(1,0)), the verifier crashes with an unhandled exception instead of reporting the illegal-HTML message, aborting the whole plugin run with a stack trace instead of a diagnostic.

[BUG] getEnglishValue catches MissingResourceException and silently returns an empty string, so a translation key missing from the English bundle is verified against an empty reference instead of being reported. Keys removed from English but still present in translations are silently checked under POLICY_NO_HTML with no anchor reference: legit HTML-bearing stale translations fail with a misleading 'Illegal HTML' message, and the actual defect (a stale orphan key) is never named, misdirecting translators who fix the wrong thing.

[ADVISORY] verifySafeHtml throws raw RuntimeException on IOException instead of the MojoExecutionException the verify() contract uses for its other read failure. A missing/unreadable English counterpart file aborts the Maven build with a raw Java stack trace rather than the plugin's normal 'Can not read file' diagnostic, and it fails fast before remaining messages are collected, so one bad path hides all other verification findings in the same run.

[ADVISORY] The 'Didn't find anchor tag X in original string' message misdescribes the common failure case where the anchor exists in English but with different attributes (e.g. missing target="_blank" or a different href). When a translator alters anchor attributes the tag WAS found in the original but does not match; the message sends them hunting for a nonexistent tag and misrepresents the check, and because the loop breaks without comparing further, remaining anchors in the same key are silently not validated.

[ADVISORY] The file is parsed twice per run — Files.readString for verifyNoDuplicateKeys and a second FileInputStream/PropertyResourceBundle for verifySafeHtml — creating two independent parses of the same resource that can drift (e.g. encoding handling). If the two readers ever disagree on decoding (PropertyResourceBundle stream vs readString charset behavior), duplicate-key checking and HTML checking validate different byte streams; the next maintainer must reason about two loaders for one file.

[ADVISORY] normalizeValue hardcodes per-key exception handling as an if/else-if chain keyed on exact key names (templateHelp, optimizeLookupHelp, error-invalid-multivalued-size), a hand-maintained parallel enumeration between message keys and verifier code. Every new key needing a format exception requires editing this chain; a missed key produces a build failure that only the author of the message change sees, and the growing key list has no single source of truth tying it to the properties files.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds HTML sanitization in `VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml()` and selects `POLICY_SOME_HTML` when the English value contains HTML (`containsHtml(englishValue)`). `POLICY_SOME_HTML` is hardcoded to allow only `br`, `p`, `strong`, and `b`, so any other tag in a translation (or in English-derived translated content) would be stripped by `policy.sanitize(value)` and then reported via `messages.add("Illegal HTML...")`. This makes the verifier intentionally restrictive and creates a maintenance/scalability concern (future legitimate strings using other tags require changing the whitelist or adding more per-key normalization exceptions), but the diff does not prove this is currently breaking correctness; it appears to be a deliberate safety policy rather than a clear defect.

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.verify(), verifySafeHtml() is invoked inside a try that only catches IOException from Files.readString(...). However, verifySafeHtml() itself catches IOExceptions when loading both the target bundle and the derived English bundle and rethrows them as raw RuntimeException (e.g., `throw new RuntimeException("unable to read file " + englishFile, e);`). That unchecked exception will escape verify() (despite its `throws MojoExecutionException` contract) and can crash the verifier without a diagnosable MojoExecutionException.
